bedtime.recovery: A very late bedtime usually means too little sleep and an irregular schedule. Deep sleep is concentrated in the first half of the night, so sleeping late makes it easier to lose deep sleep.
tips: Move it 15–30 minutes earlier at a time, hold for a week, then move again
Dim the lights and put the phone away an hour before bed
bedtime.title: Bedtime
bedtime.what: Average start time of the main sleep over the last 7 nights.

behavior.recovery: Correlation, not causation, but logging consistently shows which habits really hold you back.
tips: Spend 10 seconds a day checking in under Journal (or tell your AI); the more days, the more accurate
behavior.title: Behaviour impact
behavior.what: For each journal behaviour (alcohol, late meals, sauna…) with at least 5 "yes" and 5 "no" days in the last 90 days, the difference in next-day average Recovery (WHOOP's Behavior Insights). A ? means the difference is not yet certain (few samples or large swings).

body_age.recovery: It changes slowly; look at the direction over months.
tips: What works best: 7+ hours of sleep, 150 minutes of cardio and two strength sessions a week, and a higher VO₂max
body_age.title: Body age
body_age.what: A "body age" converted from 8 sleep, activity and fitness metrics, computed weekly (WHOOP Age / Healthspan).

body_battery.recovery: When the battery is already low in the afternoon, hard training in the evening pushes the next day's Recovery down further.
tips: Battery low: swap hard training for easy cardio or stretching
body_battery.title: Body battery (estimate)
body_battery.what: A rough estimate modelled on Garmin Body Battery: on waking = 20 + 75 × Recovery %, then drained each hour by time awake, stress and the day's strain. Apple Watch has no continuous daytime HRV, so it is only an estimate.

chronotype.recovery: Late chronotypes who force early rising build sleep debt; to move your schedule earlier, shift it gradually with morning sunlight and a fixed wake time.
tips: Move your wake time only 15–30 minutes earlier per week
Dim the lights in the evening
chronotype.title: Chronotype
chronotype.what: The sleep midpoint on free days (waking on Saturday or Sunday) over the last 60 nights, corrected for the sleep difference between workdays and free days (MSFsc from the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire, MCTQ).

hr_recovery.recovery: A faster drop means the parasympathetic system takes over sooner and cardiorespiratory fitness is better; a value that stays low is a cardiovascular risk signal.
tips: Don't take the watch off right after training; stand or walk slowly for 2 minutes
hr_recovery.title: Heart rate recovery
hr_recovery.what: How far your heart rate drops in the first minute after exercise (Apple's Cardio Recovery). Uses Apple Health's value first; otherwise computed from raw heart rate around the end of the workout.

hrv.recovery: The most important Recovery input (60% weight): the higher your HRV relative to your own baseline, the higher Recovery. It varies a lot between people (age, genetics), so don't compare with others; watch the 7-day average against your baseline.
tips: Keep a regular schedule and sleep 7+ hours
No alcohol or big meals within 3 hours of bed
Lower values 1–2 days after hard training are normal
Low for several days with a rising resting HR: you may be getting sick; cut back and rest
hrv.title: HRV (heart rate variability)
hrv.what: The variation between consecutive heartbeats (ms). Apple Watch records SDNN, mostly during sleep and at rest. High HRV means the parasympathetic system (rest and digest) dominates: you are relaxed and recovering well. It drops with stress, fatigue, short sleep, alcohol and illness.

hrv_status.recovery: Much steadier than a single night's HRV: a night or two of swings doesn't matter; only when the 7-day average leaves the band has fatigue or stress built up.
tips: Low: cut back for 2–3 days, sleep enough, rule out alcohol and illness
hrv_status.title: HRV status
hrv_status.what: Where your 7-day average HRV falls relative to your own baseline band of the previous 60 days (mean ± 1 SD) (Garmin's HRV Status).

illness.recovery: When several of these get worse together, your body is more likely fighting an infection or overly fatigued; Recovery is usually low too.
tips: Watch / high: only light activity that day, sleep more, drink more water
High for 2–3 days or with symptoms: rest, and see a GP if needed
illness.title: Illness risk
illness.what: Combines a rise in resting HR, a drop in HRV, a rise in respiratory rate (all against your own baseline), a rise in wrist temperature and low night-time blood oxygen into a 0–100 score, similar to Oura's Symptom Radar. It is a signal, not a diagnosis.

recovery.recovery: Green: your body is ready for high strain. Yellow: train as planned, don't push to your limit. Red: mostly easy activity and rest. Compare only with yourself; day-to-day swings are normal, adjust only after several low days in a row.
tips: 2–3 red days in a row: cut back or rest, and check sleep, alcohol and illness first
Even when green, don't stack many hard days; plan rest days
recovery.title: Recovery
recovery.what: A 0–100 score computed each morning from last night's HRV, resting HR, sleep performance and respiratory rate, compared with your own baseline of the last 60 days. Weights: HRV 60%, resting HR 20%, sleep performance 15%, respiratory rate 5%. Matching your baseline gives about 57.

recovery_time.recovery: You can train before you have fully recovered, but avoid the same muscle groups and high intensity.
tips: Still recovering: train other body parts or do Zone 2
recovery_time.title: Recovery time (estimate)
recovery_time.what: Modelled on Garmin Recovery Time: from the highest-strain day of the last 4 days, each strain point above 8 needs 5 hours, adjusted for fatigue (TSB) and today's Recovery colour; shows the hours left as of 7 am today.

resp_rate.recovery: One of the Recovery inputs (5% weight). A sudden rise is common with fever, respiratory infection, alcohol or overtraining.
tips: Clearly high two nights in a row: watch for a cold, cut back and rest
Less alcohol before bed
resp_rate.title: Respiratory rate
resp_rate.what: Breaths per minute during sleep (the median the watch measures overnight). Adults are usually at 12–20, and each person's value is very stable night to night.

resting_hr.recovery: One of the Recovery inputs (20% weight): lower than baseline is better. More than 5 bpm above baseline together with lower HRV is common with fatigue, short sleep, dehydration, alcohol or early illness. Most adults are at 60–100 bpm; 40–60 is common in people who train regularly.
tips: Drink enough water; rehydrate after sauna and training
Less alcohol at night; don't eat dinner too late or too much
Regular aerobic training (Zone 2) lowers it slowly over time
resting_hr.title: Resting HR
resting_hr.what: Heartbeats per minute when fully relaxed (bpm), lowest during sleep. "Last night's resting HR" here is the average of the lowest 5 minutes of sleep. The better your aerobic fitness, the lower it usually is.

sleep_consistency.recovery: With a stable body clock you sleep deeper and fall asleep more easily; shifting times are like daily jet lag.
tips: Fix your wake time first; bedtime will follow
On weekends don't get up more than 1 hour later than usual
sleep_consistency.title: Sleep consistency
sleep_consistency.what: How stable your bedtime and wake time are (compared with the previous 14 nights; within 15 minutes costs nothing).

sleep_debt.recovery: The more sleep debt, the harder it is to recover. Pay it back by going to bed earlier and sleeping a bit more over the next few nights, not with one long lie-in.
tips: Go to bed 30 minutes earlier for the next few nights
Keep daytime naps to 20–30 minutes and before 3 pm
sleep_debt.title: Sleep debt
sleep_debt.what: Weighted average of how much less than 8 hours you slept on each of the last 14 nights (recent nights weigh more; extra sleep pays part of it back). It is added to tonight's sleep need (up to +2 hours).

sleep_efficiency.recovery: Low efficiency means time in bed isn't turning into real sleep, so recovery suffers.
tips: Go to bed only when sleepy; use the bed only for sleep
Can't sleep for more than 20 minutes: get up, do something quiet, return when sleepy
Avoid screens and bright light in the last hour before bed
sleep_efficiency.title: Sleep efficiency
sleep_efficiency.what: Time asleep ÷ time in bed. Scrolling in bed, taking long to fall asleep and long awakenings all lower it.

sleep_hours.recovery: Adults need 7–9 hours a night, more with heavy training. Short sleep lowers HRV, raises resting HR and builds sleep debt; it also increases appetite and hurts strength gains and fat loss.
tips: Fix your wake time first (weekends too), then move bedtime earlier step by step
Get sunlight within 30 minutes of waking
No coffee after noon; finish training at least 3 hours before bed
Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet
sleep_hours.title: Sleep duration
sleep_hours.what: Time actually asleep (not time lying awake in bed), from the watch's sleep stages.

sleep_perf_whoop.recovery: More complete than duration alone: enough sleep at irregular times or with many awakenings still pulls the score down.
tips: Consistency pulling it down: fix your wake time
Efficiency pulling it down: go to bed only when sleepy
sleep_perf_whoop.title: Sleep performance (combined)
sleep_perf_whoop.what: A combined score modelled on WHOOP's newer Sleep Performance: meeting your sleep need 60% + consistency 20% + sleep efficiency 20% (WHOOP also uses sleep stress, which we have no data for, so its weight goes to the other three). For comparison only; not a Recovery input.

sleep_score.recovery: A low sleep score usually means low Recovery too. Find the part pulling the score down and fix that first.
tips: Low consistency: sleep and wake at the same time every day
Low duration: secure 7 hours first
Many awakenings: less water and alcohol before bed, a cooler bedroom
sleep_score.title: Sleep score
sleep_score.what: 0–100, four weighted parts: duration 40% (7–9 hours scores full), sleep stages 20% (enough deep and REM sleep), consistency 20% (how far bedtime is from the previous 14 nights) and interruptions 20%.

spo2.recovery: Not a Recovery input; used for the illness signal. Repeated low values at night can be linked to sleep apnoea, a cold or altitude; readings depend on how snugly the watch is worn.
tips: One low night is usually a fit problem
Low for a long time with snoring and daytime sleepiness: ask your GP for a sleep assessment
spo2.title: Blood oxygen (SpO₂)
spo2.what: The share of oxygenated haemoglobin in the blood, measured intermittently by the watch during sleep. Usually 95–100% in healthy people.

steps.recovery: Everyday activity (NEAT) is a big part of fat loss; a sedentary day doesn't necessarily mean higher Recovery.
tips: Walk 10–15 minutes after meals; it also helps blood sugar and triglycerides
steps.title: Steps
steps.what: Steps per day (WHOOP shows them too since 5.0).

strain.recovery: Match strain to Recovery: on green days you can go above 14, on red days stay under 10. Recovery usually drops the day after high strain.
tips: Strength training keeps heart rate low, so strain reads low; look at muscle load
After several high-strain days, plan a low-strain day
strain.title: Strain
strain.what: How much cardiovascular load you took on in a day, 0–21, converted from the time your heart rate spent in each zone (TRIMP); the higher it gets, the harder it is to raise.

strain_combined.recovery: Strength training keeps heart rate low, so cardiovascular strain alone underestimates days like leg day.
tips: Don't schedule too many strength days and hard cardio days back to back
strain_combined.title: Strain (incl. muscle)
strain_combined.what: An optional definition: cardiovascular TRIMP plus the muscle load of strength training (your median session of the last 90 days ≈ 60 TRIMP), converted to 0–21, similar to how WHOOP counts Strength Trainer in Strain. It does not replace the main strain.

read: Training too little for a long time
training_status.recovery: Overreaching or strained: cut back first. Detraining: build your training volume back up gradually.
tips: Low aerobic making up most of the load is normal (the 80/20 rule)
To raise VO₂max: add one high-intensity interval session a week
training_status.title: Training status
training_status.what: Training effect judged from the acute:chronic workload ratio (7 / 28 days), HRV status and the 60-day change in VO₂max (similar to Garmin Training Status / Polar training load status). The load focus below is the share of 28-day TRIMP at low aerobic (50–70%), high aerobic (70–90%) and anaerobic (≥ 90% HRmax) intensity.

read: Top 20% for your age and sex
vo2max.recovery: Not a Recovery input; it is a long-term marker: higher VO₂max goes with a lower resting HR and faster recovery, and is strongly linked to longevity and cardiovascular health. It changes slowly; look at trends over months.
tips: 2–3 Zone 2 cardio sessions a week (you can talk but not sing, e.g. incline walking), 30–60 minutes each
One interval session a week (e.g. 4×4 minutes hard with 3 minutes easy walking in between)
Losing fat by itself raises it (it is per kg of body weight)
vo2max.title: VO₂max (maximal oxygen uptake)
vo2max.what: The most oxygen your body can use per kilogram of body weight per minute at full effort (mL/kg·min), a measure of cardiorespiratory fitness. Apple Watch estimates it during outdoor walks, runs and hikes.

weight.recovery: Losing weight too fast (too big a calorie deficit) often comes with fatigue, early waking, lower strength and falling Recovery.
tips: Weigh every morning after the toilet, before eating or drinking
Adjust calories by the weekly average, not single days
weight.title: Weight
weight.what: Your latest weigh-in (manual entries first). Look at the 7-day average: water, salt, carbs and bowel movements can shift a single day by 1–2 kg.

bedtime.recovery: 入睡太晚通常意味着睡不够、作息不规律，深睡集中在前半夜，晚睡更容易丢掉深睡。
tips: 每次只提前 15–30 分钟，稳定一周再提前
睡前 1 小时调暗灯光、放下手机
bedtime.title: 入睡时间
bedtime.what: 近 7 晚主睡眠开始时间的平均。

behavior.recovery: 是相关不是因果，但持续记录后能看出哪些习惯真的在拖累你。
tips: 每天花 10 秒在「日记」里打卡（或对你的 AI 说一句），越多越准
behavior.title: 行为影响
behavior.what: 日记里每个行为（喝酒、晚吃、桑拿……）近 90 天「是」和「否」各至少 5 天时，比较第二天恢复分的平均差（WHOOP 的 Behavior Insights）。带 ? 的是差别还不够确定（样本少或波动大）。

body_age.recovery: 变化很慢，看几个月的方向。
tips: 最有效的是：睡够 7 小时、每周 150 分钟有氧、两次力量、VO₂max 提高
body_age.title: 身体年龄
body_age.what: 用睡眠、活动、体能 8 项指标换算的「身体年龄」，每周算一次（WHOOP Age / Healthspan）。

body_battery.recovery: 下午电量已经很低时，晚上的高强度训练会进一步压低第二天的恢复。
tips: 电量低：把高强度换成轻松有氧或拉伸
body_battery.title: 身体电量（估算）
body_battery.what: 仿 Garmin Body Battery 的粗略估算：醒来时 = 20 + 75 × 恢复分%，之后每小时按清醒、压力和当天负荷扣减。Apple Watch 白天没有连续 HRV，所以只是估算。

chronotype.recovery: 生物钟偏晚的人硬早起会欠睡眠债；想把作息往前挪，要靠早上晒太阳和固定起床时间慢慢推。
tips: 每周只把起床提前 15–30 分钟
晚上调暗灯光
chronotype.title: 生物钟类型
chronotype.what: 近 60 晚休息日（周六、周日醒来）的睡眠中点，按平时和休息日的睡眠差校正（慕尼黑时型问卷 MCTQ 的 MSFsc）。

hr_recovery.recovery: 下降越快说明副交感神经越快接管，心肺能力越好；长期偏低是心血管风险信号。
tips: 训练结束后别马上摘表，站着或慢走 2 分钟
hr_recovery.title: 运动后心率恢复
hr_recovery.what: 运动结束后 1 分钟心率下降了多少（Apple 的 Cardio Recovery）。优先用 Apple 健康的数值，没有时用训练结束前后的原始心率自己算。

hrv.recovery: 恢复分最重要的输入（权重 60%）：HRV 相对你自己的基线越高，恢复分越高。个体差异很大（年龄、遗传），不要和别人比，看 7 天均值相对基线的变化。
tips: 规律作息、睡够 7 小时以上
睡前 3 小时内不喝酒、不吃大餐
高强度训练后 1–2 天偏低是正常的
连续几天偏低且静息心率升高：可能是生病前兆，减量休息
hrv.title: HRV 心率变异性
hrv.what: 相邻两次心跳间隔的波动（毫秒）。Apple Watch 记录的是 SDNN，多在睡眠和安静时测。HRV 高说明副交感神经（休息、消化）占主导，身体放松、恢复得好；压力、疲劳、睡眠不足、饮酒、生病时会下降。

hrv_status.recovery: 比单晚 HRV 稳定得多：一两晚波动不要紧，7 天均值掉出带外才说明身体累积了疲劳或压力。
tips: 偏低：减量 2–3 天、睡够，排查饮酒和生病
hrv_status.title: HRV 状态
hrv_status.what: 最近 7 天 HRV 均值落在你自己前 60 天基线带（均值 ± 1 个标准差）的哪里（Garmin 的 HRV Status）。

illness.recovery: 几项一起变差时更可能是身体在对抗感染或过度疲劳，恢复分通常也会偏低。
tips: 留意 / 高：当天只做轻活动，多睡、多喝水
连续 2–3 天高或有症状：休息，必要时看 GP
illness.title: 生病风险
illness.what: 把静息心率升高、HRV 下降、呼吸频率升高（都和你自己的基线比）、手腕温度升高、夜间血氧偏低合成 0–100 分，类似 Oura 的 Symptom Radar。只是信号提示，不是诊断。

recovery.recovery: 绿：身体准备好承受高负荷；黄：按计划练、别冲极限；红：以轻松活动和休息为主。只和自己比，单日波动正常，连续几天偏低才要调整。
tips: 连续 2–3 天红：减量或休息，先查睡眠、饮酒、生病
绿也别连续多天大负荷，安排好休息日
recovery.title: 恢复分
recovery.what: 每天早上用昨晚的 HRV、静息心率、睡眠表现和呼吸频率，和你自己近 60 天的基线比较算出的 0–100 分。权重：HRV 60%、静息心率 20%、睡眠表现 15%、呼吸频率 5%。和基线持平约 57 分。

recovery_time.recovery: 还没恢复完时可以练，但避开同一肌群和高强度。
tips: 还在恢复：换练其他部位或做 Zone 2
recovery_time.title: 恢复时间（估算）
recovery_time.what: 仿 Garmin Recovery Time：最近 4 天里负荷最高的一天，strain 每超过 8 一分要 5 小时，再按疲劳（TSB）和今天的恢复颜色调整，算到今天早上 7 点还剩多少小时。

resp_rate.recovery: 恢复分的输入之一（权重 5%）。突然升高常见于发烧、呼吸道感染、饮酒或过度训练。
tips: 连续两晚明显偏高：留意是否感冒，减量休息
睡前少喝酒
resp_rate.title: 呼吸频率
resp_rate.what: 睡眠时每分钟呼吸次数（手表夜间测得的中位数）。成人一般 12–20 次，个人每晚很稳定。

resting_hr.recovery: 恢复分的输入之一（权重 20%）：比基线越低越好。比基线高 5 bpm 以上同时 HRV 下降，常见于疲劳、睡眠不足、脱水、饮酒或生病早期。一般成人 60–100 bpm，常训练的人 40–60 也常见。
tips: 多喝水，桑拿和训练后补液
晚上少喝酒、晚餐别太晚太撑
长期规律有氧（Zone 2）能让它慢慢下降
resting_hr.title: 静息心率
resting_hr.what: 完全放松时每分钟心跳次数（bpm），夜里睡着时最低。这里的「昨晚静息心率」是睡眠中最低 5 分钟的平均。有氧能力越好，静息心率通常越低。

sleep_consistency.recovery: 生物钟稳定时睡得更深、更容易入睡；时间来回变就像每天倒时差。
tips: 先固定起床时间，入睡时间会慢慢跟上
周末起床别比平时晚 1 小时以上
sleep_consistency.title: 睡眠规律性
sleep_consistency.what: 每天入睡、起床时间稳不稳定（和前 14 晚相比，差 15 分钟以内不扣分）。

sleep_debt.recovery: 睡眠债越多，恢复越难。还债靠接下来几晚早点睡、多睡一点，不靠一次补觉。
tips: 接下来几晚每晚提前 30 分钟上床
白天小睡控制在 20–30 分钟、下午 3 点前
sleep_debt.title: 睡眠债
sleep_debt.what: 近 14 晚每晚比 8 小时少睡的部分加权平均（越近的晚上权重越大，多睡可以抵掉一部分）。会加到今晚的睡眠需求里（最多 +2 小时）。

sleep_efficiency.recovery: 效率低说明在床上的时间没有变成有效睡眠，恢复打折扣。
tips: 困了再上床，床只用来睡觉
睡不着超过 20 分钟就起来做点安静的事，困了再回去
睡前 1 小时远离屏幕和强光
sleep_efficiency.title: 睡眠效率
sleep_efficiency.what: 睡着的时间 ÷ 在床上的时间。躺着刷手机、迟迟睡不着、半夜醒很久都会拉低它。

sleep_hours.recovery: 成人建议每晚 7–9 小时，训练量大时需要更多。睡不够会压低 HRV、抬高静息心率、累积睡眠债，还会让食欲变大、力量和减脂效果变差。
tips: 先固定起床时间（周末也一样），再逐步把入睡提前
起床 30 分钟内晒太阳
午后不喝咖啡，训练在睡前 3 小时前结束
卧室凉、暗、安静
sleep_hours.title: 睡眠时长
sleep_hours.what: 实际睡着的时间（不算躺在床上醒着的时间），来自手表的睡眠阶段。

sleep_perf_whoop.recovery: 比单看时长更全面：睡得够但时间乱、半夜醒得多，分数也会被拉低。
tips: 规律性拉分：固定起床时间
效率拉分：困了再上床
sleep_perf_whoop.title: 睡眠表现（综合）
sleep_perf_whoop.what: 仿 WHOOP 新版 Sleep Performance 的综合分：睡够需求 60% + 规律性 20% + 睡眠效率 20%（WHOOP 还有睡眠压力一项，这里没有数据，权重分给其他三项）。只是对照用，不进恢复分。

sleep_score.recovery: 睡眠分低通常意味着恢复分也会低。看哪一项拉低了分数，就先改那一项。
tips: 规律性分低：每天同一时间睡和起
时长分低：先保证 7 小时
醒来多：睡前少喝水和酒，卧室别太热
sleep_score.title: 睡眠分
sleep_score.what: 0–100 分，四项加权：时长 40%（7–9 小时满分）、睡眠阶段 20%（深睡和 REM 够不够）、规律性 20%（入睡时间和前 14 晚差多少）、中途醒来 20%。

spo2.recovery: 不进恢复分，用于生病提示。夜间反复偏低可能和睡眠呼吸暂停、感冒、高原有关；手表读数受佩戴松紧影响。
tips: 偶尔一晚偏低多半是佩戴问题
长期偏低且打鼾、白天困：找 GP 做睡眠评估
spo2.title: 血氧
spo2.what: 血液里氧合血红蛋白的比例，手表在睡眠时间断测量。健康人通常 95–100%。

steps.recovery: 日常活动（NEAT）是减脂里很大的一块，久坐日恢复分不一定高。
tips: 饭后走 10–15 分钟，对血糖和甘油三酯也有好处
steps.title: 步数

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「生病风险」（10-20 需要留意 · 2）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

tips: 留意 / 高：当天只做轻活动，多睡、多喝水

metric.title: 生病风险
metric.what: 把静息心率升高、HRV 下降、呼吸频率升高（都和你自己的基线比）、手腕温度升高、夜间血氧偏低合成 0–100 分，类似 Oura 的 Symptom Radar。只是信号提示，不是诊断。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Illness risk" (20 Oct 需要留意 · 2): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?

tips: Watch / high: only light activity that day, sleep more, drink more water
High for 2–3 days or with symptoms: rest, and see a GP if needed
metric.title: Illness risk
metric.what: Combines a rise in resting HR, a drop in HRV, a rise in respiratory rate (all against your own baseline), a rise in wrist temperature and low night-time blood oxygen into a 0–100 score, similar to Oura's Symptom Radar. It is a signal, not a diagnosis.

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「身体电量（估算）」（10-20 45）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

metric.title: 身体电量（估算）
metric.what: 仿 Garmin Body Battery 的粗略估算：醒来时 = 20 + 75 × 恢复分%，之后每小时按清醒、压力和当天负荷扣减。Apple Watch 白天没有连续 HRV，所以只是估算。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Body battery (estimate)" (20 Oct 45): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?

tips: Battery low: swap hard training for easy cardio or stretching
metric.title: Body battery (estimate)
metric.what: A rough estimate modelled on Garmin Body Battery: on waking = 20 + 75 × Recovery %, then drained each hour by time awake, stress and the day's strain. Apple Watch has no continuous daytime HRV, so it is only an estimate.

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「恢复时间（估算）」（10-20 30 小时）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

tips: 还在恢复：换练其他部位或做 Zone 2
metric.title: 恢复时间（估算）
metric.what: 仿 Garmin Recovery Time：最近 4 天里负荷最高的一天，strain 每超过 8 一分要 5 小时，再按疲劳（TSB）和今天的恢复颜色调整，算到今天早上 7 点还剩多少小时。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Recovery time (estimate)" (20 Oct 30 h): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?
metric.recovery: You can train before you have fully recovered, but avoid the same muscle groups and high intensity.
tips: Still recovering: train other body parts or do Zone 2
metric.title: Recovery time (estimate)
metric.what: Modelled on Garmin Recovery Time: from the highest-strain day of the last 4 days, each strain point above 8 needs 5 hours, adjusted for fatigue (TSB) and today's Recovery colour; shows the hours left as of 7 am today.

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「运动后心率恢复」（10-20 25 bpm；30 天均 21 bpm；前 30 天 20 bpm）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

tips: 训练结束后别马上摘表，站着或慢走 2 分钟
metric.title: 运动后心率恢复
metric.what: 运动结束后 1 分钟心率下降了多少（Apple 的 Cardio Recovery）。优先用 Apple 健康的数值，没有时用训练结束前后的原始心率自己算。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Heart rate recovery" (20 Oct 25 bpm; 30-day avg 21 bpm; Previous 30 days 20 bpm): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?
metric.recovery: A faster drop means the parasympathetic system takes over sooner and cardiorespiratory fitness is better; a value that stays low is a cardiovascular risk signal.
tips: Don't take the watch off right after training; stand or walk slowly for 2 minutes
metric.title: Heart rate recovery
metric.what: How far your heart rate drops in the first minute after exercise (Apple's Cardio Recovery). Uses Apple Health's value first; otherwise computed from raw heart rate around the end of the workout.

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「负荷（含肌肉）」（10-20 12.3）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？
metric.recovery: 力量训练心率不高，只看心血管 strain 会低估练腿这种日子的负担。
tips: 力量日和高强度有氧日别连着排太多
metric.title: 负荷（含肌肉）
metric.what: 可选口径：心血管 TRIMP 加上力量训练的肌肉负荷（你近 90 天的中位训练量 ≈ 60 TRIMP）再换算成 0–21，类似 WHOOP 把 Strength Trainer 计入 Strain。不替换主页面的 strain。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Strain (incl. muscle)" (20 Oct 12.3): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?
metric.recovery: Strength training keeps heart rate low, so cardiovascular strain alone underestimates days like leg day.
tips: Don't schedule too many strength days and hard cardio days back to back
metric.title: Strain (incl. muscle)
metric.what: An optional definition: cardiovascular TRIMP plus the muscle load of strength training (your median session of the last 90 days ≈ 60 TRIMP), converted to 0–21, similar to how WHOOP counts Strength Trainer in Strain. It does not replace the main strain.

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「HRV 状态」（10-20 平衡）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？
metric.recovery: 比单晚 HRV 稳定得多：一两晚波动不要紧，7 天均值掉出带外才说明身体累积了疲劳或压力。
tips: 偏低：减量 2–3 天、睡够，排查饮酒和生病
metric.title: HRV 状态
metric.what: 最近 7 天 HRV 均值落在你自己前 60 天基线带（均值 ± 1 个标准差）的哪里（Garmin 的 HRV Status）。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "HRV status" (20 Oct 平衡): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?
metric.recovery: Much steadier than a single night's HRV: a night or two of swings doesn't matter; only when the 7-day average leaves the band has fatigue or stress built up.
tips: Low: cut back for 2–3 days, sleep enough, rule out alcohol and illness
metric.title: HRV status
metric.what: Where your 7-day average HRV falls relative to your own baseline band of the previous 60 days (mean ± 1 SD) (Garmin's HRV Status).

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「训练状态」（10-20 过度）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

read.label: 负荷合适但 HRV 偏低

metric.recovery: 过度或疲劳时先减量；去适应说明需要逐步把训练量加回来。
tips: 低有氧占大头是正常的（80/20 原则）
想提高 VO₂max：每周加一次高强度间歇
metric.title: 训练状态
metric.what: 综合急慢性负荷比（7 / 28 天）、HRV 状态和 VO₂max 60 天变化判断的训练效果（类似 Garmin Training Status / Polar 负荷状态）。下面的负荷重点是 28 天 TRIMP 在低有氧（50–70%）、高有氧（70–90%）、无氧（≥ 90% HRmax）的占比。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Training status" (20 Oct 过度): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?

metric.recovery: Overreaching or strained: cut back first. Detraining: build your training volume back up gradually.
tips: Low aerobic making up most of the load is normal (the 80/20 rule)
To raise VO₂max: add one high-intensity interval session a week
metric.title: Training status
metric.what: Training effect judged from the acute:chronic workload ratio (7 / 28 days), HRV status and the 60-day change in VO₂max (similar to Garmin Training Status / Polar training load status). The load focus below is the share of 28-day TRIMP at low aerobic (50–70%), high aerobic (70–90%) and anaerobic (≥ 90% HRmax) intensity.

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「生物钟类型」（10-20 夜猫子）：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

tips: 每周只把起床提前 15–30 分钟
晚上调暗灯光
metric.title: 生物钟类型
metric.what: 近 60 晚休息日（周六、周日醒来）的睡眠中点，按平时和休息日的睡眠差校正（慕尼黑时型问卷 MCTQ 的 MSFsc）。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Chronotype" (20 Oct 夜猫子): what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?
metric.recovery: Late chronotypes who force early rising build sleep debt; to move your schedule earlier, shift it gradually with morning sunlight and a fixed wake time.
tips: Move your wake time only 15–30 minutes earlier per week
Dim the lights in the evening
metric.title: Chronotype
metric.what: The sleep midpoint on free days (waking on Saturday or Sunday) over the last 60 nights, corrected for the sleep difference between workdays and free days (MSFsc from the Munich ChronoType Questionnaire, MCTQ).

metric.ai_prompt: 帮我解读一下我的「睡眠表现（综合）」：这是什么意思、我现在的情况怎么样、接下来具体该怎么做、要避免什么？

效率拉分：困了再上床
metric.title: 睡眠表现（综合）
metric.what: 仿 WHOOP 新版 Sleep Performance 的综合分：睡够需求 60% + 规律性 20% + 睡眠效率 20%（WHOOP 还有睡眠压力一项，这里没有数据，权重分给其他三项）。只是对照用，不进恢复分。

metric.ai_prompt: Please explain my "Sleep performance (combined)": what does it mean, how am I doing right now, what exactly should I do next, and what should I avoid?

metric.recovery: More complete than duration alone: enough sleep at irregular times or with many awakenings still pulls the score down.
tips: Consistency pulling it down: fix your wake time
Efficiency pulling it down: go to bed only when sleepy
metric.title: Sleep performance (combined)
metric.what: A combined score modelled on WHOOP's newer Sleep Performance: meeting your sleep need 60% + consistency 20% + sleep efficiency 20% (WHOOP also uses sleep stress, which we have no data for, so its weight goes to the other three). For comparison only; not a Recovery input.
